items.name: faq-anim-001
items.title: FAQ с зацикленным раскрытием
items.description: Полноценная секция вопросов и ответов в две колонки: заголовок и подводка слева, список вопросов справа. Пункты раскрываются по одному и закрываются перед следующим по кругу — без единой строки JS, только grid-template-rows и вращение шеврона на CSS.
items.docs: Секция самодостаточна: один файл, ноль зависимостей, палитра в локальных --vibeui-faq-anim-001-*. Тему берёт из окружения через light-dark() плюс строку для класса .dark. container-type делает блок собственным query-контейнером: от 56rem включается двухколоночная раскладка со sticky-заголовком слева. Раскрытие пунктов — зацикленная демонстрация на чистом CSS: пять именованных keyframes (по одному на первые пять вопросов) двигают grid-template-rows панели с 0fr до 1fr и синхронно вращают шеврон на 180deg, каждый в своей пятой доле пятнадцатисекундного круга. autoplay={false} и prefers-reduced-motion останавливают цикл и оставляют первый вопрос статично раскрытым.

en.title: FAQ with a looping reveal
en.description: A full two-column FAQ section: heading and lead copy on the left, question list on the right. Items open one at a time and close before the next in a loop — no JavaScript at all, just grid-template-rows and a CSS chevron rotation.
en.docs: The section is self-contained: one file, zero dependencies, palette in local --vibeui-faq-anim-001-* variables. It takes the theme from the environment via light-dark() plus a rule for the .dark class. container-type makes the block its own query container: a two-column layout with a sticky left heading kicks in from 56rem. The reveal is a looping CSS-only demo: five named keyframes (one per first five questions) move the panel's grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr and rotate the chevron 180deg in sync, each owning its fifth of a fifteen-second loop. autoplay={false} and prefers-reduced-motion stop the loop and leave the first question statically open.

ai.summary: A full-width FAQ section: heading and lead copy on the left, accordion on the right. Accordion items open one at a time and close before the next in an endless loop — a CSS-only demo, no client JS.

props.title: How it works, in short
props.description: Can't find an answer here? Write to us, we reply within one business day.

items.question: What do I get after installing a block?
items.answer: One file in your project — the exact same one you saw in the preview. No build step, no wrappers, no lock-in to our theme: the block carries its own palette and works in any React project.

items.question: Does the agent really install this exact component?
items.answer: Yes. Copy for AI gives a link with instructions: the component id, the install command, and a list of what not to change. The agent downloads the file from the registry instead of recreating something similar from a description.

items.question: What if I already have my own design system?
items.answer: Override the block's local variables and it will fit your theme without touching the rest of the project. No need to edit the file itself: colors, radii and accents live in variables.

items.question: Do I need extra libraries?
items.answer: Dependencies are declared in each block's metadata, and most have zero: only React. No icon library is required — icons are drawn in CSS.

items.question: Can I use blocks in commercial projects?
items.answer: Yes. After installation the file belongs to your project: edit it, rename it, and ship it with your site.
